title: From Original AHB to AHB-Lite and AHB5
description: Open each topic to separate actual interface changes from features that remained or became optional AHB5 properties.

signals.name: Interface topology
signals.description: Original AMBA 2 AHB defines a shared bus with multiple masters and centralized arbitration. AHB-Lite and AHB5 define one master per interface; a system can still connect many such interfaces through an interconnect.
signals.sampled: Ownership changes only at legal accepted-transfer boundaries
signals.verificationNote: Choose assertions from the actual interface revision. Do not expect HBUSREQ/HGRANT on an AHB-Lite or AHB5 master interface.

signals.name: Response encoding
signals.description: Original AHB uses a two-bit response encoding for OKAY, ERROR, RETRY, and SPLIT. RETRY requests a later reattempt without HSPLITx; SPLIT also removes the master from eligibility until the slave's HSPLITx indication allows it to retry. AHB-Lite and AHB5 retain only OKAY and ERROR on one-bit HRESP.
signals.sampled: With HREADY HIGH for completion; ERROR uses its required two-cycle sequence
signals.verificationNote: Keep RETRY and SPLIT state machines separate. Never decode either legacy value on a one-bit AHB-Lite/AHB5 HRESP.

signals.name: Secure_Transfers
signals.description: When the AHB5 Secure_Transfers property is True, HNONSEC is added and identifies the accepted address phase as Secure or Non-secure.
signals.direction: Master → decoder, interconnect, and selected target
signals.verificationNote: Check adapters between interfaces that do and do not declare Secure_Transfers; never invent a default security state.

signals.name: Exclusive_Transfers
signals.description: When Exclusive_Transfers is True, AHB5 adds exclusive request, identity, and success signaling so a monitor can accept or reject a conditional write without locking the whole bus.
signals.sampled: Exclusive address phase uses NONSEQ; result is sampled on completion
signals.verificationNote: Matching read/write attributes include address, size, protection, burst, master identity, and HNONSEC when applicable.

signals.name: Extended memory types
signals.description: AHB5 can extend HPROT with memory-type information when Extended_Memory_Types is declared.
signals.verificationNote: Gate checks by the declared interface property; optional signals must not be assumed universally present.

signals.name: HMASTLOCK
signals.description: AHB5 still defines HMASTLOCK. Exclusive transfers are an additional conditional-atomic mechanism, not a deletion or automatic replacement of locked sequences.
signals.direction: Address-phase indication to the selected target/interconnect
signals.verificationNote: Verify locking and exclusives independently; HEXCL does not imply HMASTLOCK.

signals.name: HMASTER
signals.expansion: The purpose changed; it was not simply removed
signals.description: Original AHB uses arbiter-generated HMASTER for shared-bus identity and SPLIT handling. AHB5 supports HMASTER when Exclusive_Transfers is True so master threads and interconnect ports can form a unique monitor identity.
signals.direction: Original arbiter or AHB5 master/interconnect → slave/monitor
values: AHB5 §8.3: HMASTER[m:0] width implementation-defined; route identity combined for uniqueness
signals.verificationNote: Track the source, configured width, thread identity, and interconnect-added route identity for the implemented revision.

signals.name: 1 KB boundary
signals.expansion: Burst restriction exists in both generations
signals.description: Original AMBA 2 AHB and AHB-Lite/AHB5 all require every AHB burst—SINGLE, incrementing, and wrapping—to remain within one 1 KB address region so it cannot cross the minimum decode boundary.
signals.sampled: Checked across every generated burst address
signals.verificationNote: A version-comparison test must not mark any burst crossing 1 KB as legal for original AHB, AHB-Lite, or AHB5.
